ready.label: Ready for Grade 4

readyWithReview.label: Ready — with a little review

notReady.label: Let's build strong roots first

sections.title: Grade 3 skills
sections.description: The most important words, reading, grammar and writing from Grade 3.

sections.title: Grade 2 skills
sections.description: Key words, reading, grammar and writing from Grade 2.

questions.question: Which word means a place where you can borrow and read books?
questions.options: hospital | garden | library | market
questions.explanation: A library is full of books you can borrow, read and bring back for others to enjoy.

questions.question: What does 'prepare' mean?
questions.options: To throw something away | To break something into pieces | To get something ready before you need it | To forget about something
questions.correctAnswer: To get something ready before you need it
questions.explanation: When you prepare, you get ready — like preparing your school bag the night before a lesson.

questions.question: Which word means a chart that shows the days, weeks and months of the year?
questions.options: eraser | border | metre | calendar
questions.explanation: A calendar shows every day and month of the year, so we can plan birthdays and holidays.

questions.question: Which word means a small town in the countryside where not many people live?
questions.options: market | college | village | hospital
questions.explanation: A village is a small place in the countryside, much smaller than a city.

questions.question: Which word tells us how hot or cold something is?
questions.options: distance | temperature | height | weight
questions.explanation: Temperature measures heat and cold — a hot day has a high temperature.

questions.question: Read this: 'Omar walks to the market with his grandfather. They buy fruit and talk to the shopkeeper. Then they rest in the garden.' Where do Omar and his grandfather rest?
questions.options: At the hospital | In the garden | At the market | At school
questions.explanation: The last sentence tells us: 'Then they rest in the garden.'

questions.question: Read this: 'Layla measured the table. It was one metre long. Her pencil was much shorter.' Which sentence is true?
questions.options: The table and the pencil are the same size. | Layla measured the chair. | The pencil is longer than the table. | The table is longer than the pencil.
questions.correctAnswer: The table is longer than the pencil.
questions.explanation: The pencil is much shorter, so the table must be longer than the pencil.

questions.question: Read this: 'At 6 o'clock, Idris wakes up and gets ready. At 7, he eats breakfast with his family. At 8, he walks to school with his neighbour Sami.' What does Idris do at 8 o'clock?
questions.options: He eats breakfast. | He wakes up. | He walks to school with Sami. | He does his chores.
questions.correctAnswer: He walks to school with Sami.
questions.explanation: The passage says that at 8 o'clock, Idris walks to school with his neighbour Sami.

questions.question: Read this: 'Nora is kind, so she helped the boy who tripped. She always tells the truth, even when it is hard, because she is honest.' Why did Nora help the boy who tripped?
questions.options: Because she was busy | Because she is kind | Because she was careless | Because she was popular
questions.explanation: The passage tells us Nora is kind, so she helped the boy who tripped.

questions.question: Read this: 'Amal had a new idea for her project. She closed her eyes and tried to imagine the finished picture before she began.' What did Amal do before she began her project?
questions.options: She imagined the finished picture. | She asked her teacher for help. | She copied a friend's picture. | She gave up on her idea.
questions.explanation: The passage says Amal closed her eyes and tried to imagine the finished picture before she began.

questions.question: Which sentence tells us what is happening right now?
questions.options: Amina will help her mother tomorrow. | Amina helped her mother yesterday. | Amina helps her mother every day. | Amina is helping her mother.
questions.explanation: The present continuous, with 'is helping', tells us about an action happening at this very moment.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: All About Me and My Family

questions.question: Choose the correct word: 'Last August, we ___ on holiday to the coast.'
questions.options: going | went | go | goes
questions.explanation: 'Went' is the past of 'go'. It is an irregular verb, so it changes instead of adding -ed.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.options: My brother is taller than me. | My brother is tallest than me. | My brother is most tall than me. | My brother is more taller than me.
questions.correctAnswer: My brother is taller than me.
questions.explanation: To compare two people we say 'taller than' — one comparative word does the whole job.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: 'I have ___ a real mountain forest.'
questions.options: seen | seeing | see | saw
questions.explanation: After 'have' we use the past participle. 'Seen' is the special past participle of 'see'.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly begins a set of instructions for making a calendar?
questions.options: You are drawing twelve squares. | First, draw twelve squares. | Drawing twelve squares. | Twelve squares you draw.
questions.explanation: Instructions begin with a command word (an imperative) like 'draw', often after a time word like 'First'.

questions.question: Choose the best joining word: 'Nora forgot her umbrella, ___ she got wet in the rain.'
questions.options: and | because | so | but
questions.explanation: 'So' shows a result — forgetting the umbrella is why Nora got wet.

questions.question: Put these steps for making a calendar in the correct order: 1) mark your special days 2) draw twelve squares 3) write one month in each square. Which order is correct?
questions.explanation: First draw the squares, then write the months inside them, and only then mark your special days.

questions.question: Which sentence is written correctly?
questions.options: amal wants to imagine a new story | Amal wants to imagine a new story. | Amal Wants To Imagine A New Story. | Amal wants to imagine a new story
questions.correctAnswer: Amal wants to imagine a new story.
questions.explanation: A name always starts with a capital letter, and every sentence ends with a full stop.

questions.question: Today is Monday. What day comes next?
questions.options: Tuesday | Friday | Saturday | Sunday
questions.explanation: The days go in order: Monday, then Tuesday.

questions.question: Which word means the day you were born, which you celebrate every year?
questions.options: birthday | weekend | calendar | date
questions.explanation: Your birthday is the day you were born, and you celebrate it once every year.

questions.question: Which word means how long something is from one end to the other?
questions.options: weight | height | length | size
questions.explanation: Length tells us how long something is, measured from one end to the other.

questions.question: Read this: 'Sara takes the bus to the city. She visits the park and eats lunch near the fountain.' How does Sara go to the city?
questions.options: By bike | On a train | In a boat | By bus
questions.explanation: The first sentence tells us: 'Sara takes the bus to the city.'

questions.question: Read this: 'The octopus has eight long arms and no bones at all. It changes its colour to hide from a hungry shark.' How does the octopus hide from a shark?
questions.options: It swims away very fast. | It changes its colour. | It grows much bigger. | It closes its eyes tight.
questions.explanation: The passage tells us the octopus changes its colour to hide from a hungry shark.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.options: The tower is more high than the house. | The tower is high than the house. | The tower is highest than the house. | The tower is higher than the house.
questions.correctAnswer: The tower is higher than the house.
questions.explanation: When we compare two things, we add -er: 'higher than the house'.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: 'This is my sister. ___ likes drawing.'
questions.options: He | She | It | They
questions.explanation: A sister is a girl, so we use 'she' to talk about her.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: 'My father ___ tea every morning.'
questions.options: like | likes | liking | liked
questions.explanation: With he, she and it we add an 's': my father likes tea.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: 'There ___ ten circles on the chart.'
questions.options: is | are | be | was
questions.explanation: Ten is more than one, so we use 'are': there are ten circles.

questions.question: Which line would you find at the very START of a postcard to a friend?
questions.options: From Amal | Dear Nora, | Tomorrow I will | The End
questions.explanation: A postcard or letter begins with a greeting, like 'Dear Nora,', and ends with your name.

questions.question: Put these directions in the correct order: 1) turn right at the bus stop 2) walk straight ahead past the market 3) turn left at the traffic light. Which order is correct?
questions.explanation: Good directions are given in the order you actually walk them: straight ahead first, then the turns that follow.

questions.question: Which sentence compares two things correctly?
questions.options: My pencil is long than my rubber. | My pencil is longer than my rubber. | My pencil is more long than my rubber. | My pencil longer than my rubber.
questions.correctAnswer: My pencil is longer than my rubber.
questions.explanation: To compare two things we add -er and use the word 'than': longer than.
